A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have engineered a microorganism with increased resistance to ionizing radioactivity, a property that is useful for bioremediation of radioactive wastes and for use in space travel.
we have shown that we can overproduce a single-stranded binding proteins, RPA, in an archaeon and that this overproduction leads to an increase in radiation resistance.
we have bioengineered a halophilic extremophile to have increased levels of radiation resistance by overexpressing the Rfa3 subunit of the RPA protein complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
overexpression of the single-stranded binding proteins Rfa3 and/or Rfa8 can increase ionizing radiation resistance and may have applications in medicine and the environment.
the overexpression of RPA in Halobacterum sp. NRC1 confers ionizing radiation resistance.
overproduction of the haloarchaeal single-stranded DNA binding protein, RPA, can be used as a strategy to engineer cells to be more tolerant of ionizing radiation.
